topics.title: [grug] Add the Hero-mix and quality-classifier fast tracks
topics.body:
* add two data fast tracks next to the model ladder. all three tracks train the same dense/MoE ladder (d512–d1280) on 8×H100 and compare on final Paloma macro loss
* model ladder: `fast-track` trains on the frozen `hero_tok/v16384_shuf/train` cache, as before
  * `launch.py` resolves the budget in `resolve_h100_ladder_budget` and takes a `TrainingSource`, so the data tracks use the same training wiring
  * add `--seed` and `--data-seed`. `--submit` forwards `WANDB_MODE` and accepts `WANDB_MODE=disabled` without `WANDB_API_KEY`
* hero mix plus a new dataset: sample the production Hero mixture and give a new Hugging Face dataset a fraction `p` of the training tokens
  * `hero_sample_cli` replays `harrier_mix_2026_08_18.json` over `store_4d2e363d` in the production loader order and retokenizes each source segment as BOS + text + EOS with `hero-bpe-v16384` into a `PreparedHeroSample`. build it once at the largest ladder budget (17,478,713,344 tokens) and use it again for all rungs
  * `add_dataset_cli` tokenizes a bounded HF prefix at an immutable revision, scales the Hero weights by `1 - p`, and caps the new data at `C = min(p·B, (N/T)·B)` to simulate the production epoch count [^1]
  * `hero_baseline_cli` trains the matched control on the same `PreparedHeroSample`
  * the Hero cell capacity check runs on the final mixture weights, so a small `p` cannot make the largest cell repeat its data
* quality classifier: sample raw text from all 292 registered sources in proportion to corpus size, score it with a frozen head, and train on the top documents
  * `corpus_sample_cli` builds a `RawCorpusPool` with `corpus-id-interval-v1`: one seeded cyclic interval in the 128-bit document-ID space for each source. it skips a row group only when its ID statistics show no overlap. `--label-exclusion-manifest` is required
  * `quality_labels_cli` freezes the GLM-5.2 labels and fits a ridge head on cached Harrier features (target `(quality - 1) / 4`, 80/10/10 split by duplicate group). the raw pool excludes all labelled duplicate groups
  * `quality_cli --stage features|score|select|train` scores the pool once at the largest rung. for budget `B`, it ranks the first `10·B` raw tokens and keeps whole documents until they fill `B`. `--selection-method candidate|incumbent|random` gives the matched controls
* the data-track CLIs default to MoE and derive `--data-seed` from `--seed`, the same as `fast-track`
* add `fast-track-long-string-v1` for HF and raw-corpus tokenization: split at the first whitespace at or after 10,000 characters, and reject a document above 64 MiB with its source and ID
  * bound native tokenizer batches by bytes. a local 32 MiB probe kept all 19,532,169 token IDs, and peak RSS went from 4.60 GiB to 2.85 GiB
* rename `max_train_batches` → `max_train_sequences` in `LmDataConfig`, so a component cap does not depend on the batch size
* fixes found during the runs
  * iris: repair missing CUDA toolchain files. put the child job and attempt in JAX coordinator names, because sibling training jobs connected to the coordinator of a different job
  * fray: pass actor concurrency to Iris RPC servers, because the 32-thread default let long waits block worker heartbeats. the inference broker sets its concurrency explicitly
  * datakit CPU drivers install the `cpu` group with `datakit`, so that they do not resolve the CUDA Torch wheel
  * artifact loading keeps absolute bucket paths, grug dispatch forwards `WANDB_MODE`, and levanter keeps eval metrics between detail intervals
* results at this time (seed 0, final macro loss from the training logs [^2])
  * hero mix, MoE, change against the Hero baseline at the same rung [^3]:

    | rung | 10% Paloma | 10% Uncheatable | 99% Paloma | 99% Uncheatable |
    |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
    | d512 | +4.22% | +1.95% | +58.70% | +68.40% |
    | d768 | +3.30% | +1.56% | +56.97% | +63.72% |
    | d1024 | +4.28% | +1.51% | +55.47% | +61.68% |
    | d1280 | not valid | not valid | +48.85% | +60.26% |

  * each valid mixed run is worse on all 23 evaluation datasets. for 10% at d512 dense, three matched seeds changed Paloma loss by +0.05%, +0.05%, and −0.14%
  * quality, four-source pilot (`cp/arxiv_abstracts`, `cp/wikiteam`, `docx-corpus/en`, `starcoder2/documentation`, 6,064,023 documents): ridge selection against random selection gave Paloma macro BPB 1.9051 against 1.6164, and 20 of 23 datasets were worse
  * these probes test the mechanics. they use assumed production counts and one seed, so they do not show the value of WikiText or of the ridge head
* open work
  * build the `resample-v2` Hero sample and run the four-scale Hero-mix comparison again on it
  * the all-292 raw pool stopped after about 14 h: `stack-v3` has documents of 79–213 MB, above the 64 MiB limit. a policy is necessary (drop and count, raise the limit, or exclude the source). no four-scale quality run exists yet
  * the 10% d1280 run resumed from a temporary checkpoint after a preemption near step 14.1k. its training loss went from 1.45 to 2.75 and did not recover, so the result is not valid. the cause is not known
  * training reads the new dataset in HF prefix order, because the Hero mixture uses `shuffle=False` and Levanter has no shuffle for one component
  * the pool excludes only the candidate's labels, not the training labels of an incumbent scorer
* remove the DataKit end-to-end track from this PR [^4]

[^1]: `N` is the number of available unique tokens in the new dataset, `T` is the production budget (default 18.75T), and `B` is the rung budget. the loader cap rounds down to whole sequences.
[^2]: these runs used W&B offline mode, so the values come from the `levanter.eval` log lines.
[^3]: these runs used the earlier resampler, which kept the source BOS as text and did not put an EOS after the last segment of a source example. the control and the treatment used the same sample, so each delta compares like with like, but the sample differs from `resample-v2`. old `PreparedHeroSample` and `PreparedAddDatasetCache` artifacts must be prepared again.
[^4]: this removes `--source-mode sample|registry`, the token-shuffle control, the shared Zephyr pool (`execution_scope`), and coordinator driver placement in the reference DataKit pipeline. the 25B-sample results and controls are in an earlier revision of this description.

topics.title: [inference] Cover June Snowball TPU parity
topics.body:
Add native checkpoint and TPU vLLM coverage for the June 67B-A2B Snowball step-42150 checkpoint. Both TPU checks use v6e-8 in us-east5 and the same [64 frozen prompts](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/test-data/vllm/e2e/representative-eval-prompts/47863868cbfe336739c8097535f113f4d2dae4954f772eb91511c911433596e8.json), split across context buckets through 32K. Native TPU restore reads checkpoint arrays directly into BF16 while preserving TensorStore memory limits and replica reads. H100 coverage remains native checkpoint, exported Levanter and vLLM at pipeline parallelism one and two; the last uses two nodes.

Keep the exported-model GPU references, native TPU reference and probability limits. TPU vLLM's maximum absolute probability error on native TPU reference tokens remains bounded by 0.04, 0.125, 0.10, 0.70 and 0.50 at 256, 1K, 4K, 16K and 32K tokens. The exact native GPU reference includes the intentional rounding correction merged in #10069.

Refresh onto maintained main, including #10069 and the mesh fix in #9401. TPU serving keeps vLLM fb02daf1 and stages the backend fixes from marin-community/tpu-inference#28, marin-community/tpu-inference#29 and marin-community/tpu-inference#27. Keep this draft until those fixes land, tpu-inference is pinned to one maintained-main commit containing all three fixes, and all six hardware checks pass at one final Marin revision. The [earlier hardware results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9400#issuecomment-6129427326) and [native GPU correction](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9400#issuecomment-6133449648) retain their recorded scope.

Supersedes #7556. Part of #8323.

Previously, vLLM could omit the tokenizer chat template advertised by the inference service. Load that template in both VllmBackend.serve() and direct start() calls and pass it to vLLM. Document that the launch-wide Evalchemy seed overrides task-file seeds and is stored in record.json under eval.evalchemy.seed.

The affected safe suite passes: 2,382 passed, 4 skipped, and 5 xfailed. This includes the 227 focused regression tests, which also pass in a separate run. Changed-file lint and full type checks pass; the advisory lint review reported no findings.

topics.title: [fast-track] Marin Belay v1: hill-climb the scaling ladder (Paloma macro loss, 8 min on 8×H100)
topics.body:
This issue tracks iterative improvements to the Marin pretraining scaling ladder (`experiments/grug/fast_track`) using the **Marin Belay** process. It is a twist on autoresearch: an agent runs experiments in batches, and anyone can steer it with research directions. > **To suggest a research direction, comment on [Marin Belay Intake (#9514)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514).** Suggestions a maintainer approves (👍 from a `marin-devs` member) are copied into this thread automatically, and the agent acts only on this thread. This thread holds the agent's batch reports and maintainer steering. ![fast_track MoE ladder: Marin 535B baseline, clean KMA and candidate 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/9697c11ef215ec0f9d536a1bceb0876f768fcf26/v1/ladder_scaling.png) The Marin 535B compute-optimal baseline follows `L(C) = 1.2 + 59.0·C^(−0.0843)` over four data-matched rungs. Clean KMA, the current baseline (★), is 0.022 lower at d512, 0.049 lower at d768, 0.040 lower at d1024 and 0.033 lower at d1280, which is about 1.14×, 1.43×, 1.40× and 1.35× the baseline's compute efficiency. Its dashed curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 64.8·C^(−0.0870)`. The **?** marks the open question this issue is chasing: how much further down each point can go. The red diamonds are the current best recipe, candidate 9 (Status below): **2.977 / 2.725 / 2.515 / 2.397** at d512 / d768 / d1024 / d1280. d512 and d768 are seed means, and the bigram table follows rule A. d768–d1280 are data-matched; d512 sits at its fixed-time step count (2817 vs 2383 steps), so it's plotted slightly to the right. That is 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.078 / 0.074 below clean KMA. Its dash-dot curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 55.0·C^(−0.0847)`. Its slope is a little shallower than clean KMA's, so the gap narrows with compute: projected to **1e24 FLOPs, 1.710 vs clean KMA's 1.727, about 1.48× clean KMA's compute efficiency and 2.95× the 535B baseline's**. Because the fixed-time d512 point flattens the fitted slope, that projection is probably conservative. The right panel is clean KMA's training MFU at each rung on one 8×H100 node: 9.5% at d512 and d768, 12.2% at d1024, and 13.0% at d1280. FLOPs are counted from KMA's own layers (KDA, MLA + Inkling, AttnRes), as 3× forward with no recompute. The trainer's logged `throughput/mfu` uses the baseline architecture's FLOP formula, so it is slightly off for KMA. ## Objective **Minimize Paloma macro loss (`eval/paloma/macro_loss`, final step) at the d512 rung after a fixed 8 minutes of 8×H100 train-step time.** - **Fixed time, not fixed tokens.** Faster code trains on more tokens within the 8 minutes, so a pure speedup counts as a win. - The LR schedule depends on the step count, so fix steps before each run: `num_steps = round(480 s × ex/s ÷ batch)`. - Measure ex/s with a short `--no-eval` probe (~30 steps) on the same cluster, and use the steady-state throughput. - Compile, evals and startup are excluded from the 8 minutes. - **Numerics changes are allowed** (e.g. FP8, precision changes, approximate kernels). They count as ordinary wins; no parity check needed. - **Noise.** Differences under ~0.005 are noise. A win must beat the current best by more than 0.005. ### Gates (both relative to the current baseline, same fixed-time rule at each rung) - **Gate 1:** beat the baseline at d512 and d768. - **Gate 2:** also beat it at d1024 and d1280, **and** project to lower Paloma macro loss at 1e24 FLOPs. Fit a power law of final loss against training FLOPs across the four rungs, for both the baseline and the variant, fixing the asymptote to 1.2. ### Fixed - Training data, the 16k BPE tokenizer, and the eval sets. - Sequence length 4096. - One 8×H100 node per rung. - The FLOP accounting used for the gate-2 projection. ### Judgment calls - **Hero-scale speed is out of scope for v1, so use discretion.** - Robust target criteria would also check training speed and inference speed at hero scale. Marin Belay v1 skips those checks. - Judge whether a change's d512 gain would carry over to hero scale, and avoid changes whose gain comes from d512-only effects. Two examples: - Dropping MoE for dense would be a clear win at d512 because dense gets ~5× higher MFU there, but that MFU gain would not carry over at hero scale. - A much larger KV cache would also be a clear win at d512, but it would hurt long-context inference speed. - **Avoid magic numbers.** - Prefer changes with few new tuned constants. A tuned constant is justified when its gain is above the noise threshold and holds as a pattern across scales. For example, a 2× LR on one parameter group qualifies if it clears the noise threshold and the gain shows up consistently at larger rungs. - The higher a change's risk of curve fitting, the more scales it must be validated at before it counts as a win. - **Spend effort in proportion to an idea's likelihood of improvement.** - Promising ideas deserve several attempts. Long shots can be tried once and dropped. - A first run is not a verdict for a large change. If you try a new architecture or component, tune its optimizer assignment, LR, init and other key hyperparameters before concluding it doesn't work. The baseline's settings were tuned for the baseline, not for the new idea. ## Architecture (current best, d512) The diagrams below show **clean KMA**. The current best recipe adds the components listed under **Status → Current best recipe**: MLA key norm and key offset, a gated bigram-memory AttnRes source, ReLU² experts, and optimizer, schedule and logit changes. The diagrams show d512; the other rungs differ in the Shape table only. **1. Layer stack and Block Attention Residuals.** Every sublayer reads its input through its own AttnRes gate, a per-token softmax over the residual history. At d512 each layer closes an AttnRes block, so the history at layer *i* is the embedding plus one sum per earlier layer. [¹](#arch-note) ```mermaid flowchart TB tok["token ids
B × 4096, packed documents"] --> emb["token embedding
16384 × 512"] emb --> en["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] en --> S0(["source 0
embedding"]) S0 --> L0 subgraph STACK["6 layers: local KDA ×4, global MLA ×2 (every 4th + last)"] direction TB L0["layer 0 · KDA + MoE"] --> L1["layer 1 · KDA + MoE"] --> L2["layer 2 · KDA + MoE"] L2 --> L3["layer 3 · MLA + Inkling + MoE"] --> L4["layer 4 · KDA + MoE"] --> L5["layer 5 · MLA + Inkling + MoE"] end L0 -. "block sum b0" .-> H L1 -. "b1" .-> H L2 -. "b2" .-> H L3 -. "b3" .-> H L4 -. "b4" .-> H S0 -.-> H H[("AttnRes history, read by every gate
[embedding, b0 … b(i−1)]
+ running partial")] L5 --> FG["final AttnRes gate
softmax over embedding, b0…b4, partial"] FG --> fn["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] fn --> head["lm_head (untied) 512 × 16384
fused CE, vocab tile 8192, z-loss 1e-4"] head --> loss(["next-token loss"]) ``` **2. One layer.** The two sublayers each have an AttnRes gate. The MoE gate also sees the attention output written just before it, as the running partial. ```mermaid flowchart TB Hin[("history
embedding + b0…b(i−1)")] --> GA subgraph GATE["AttnRes gate (one per sublayer, 13 at d512)"] direction TB GA["logit_n = q · rms_norm(source_n)
q ∈ ℝ⁵¹², zero-init (uniform mix)
frozen key norm"] --> SM["softmax over sources
weighted sum of raw sources"] end SM --> A1["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] --> MIX{{"mixer
KDA (local) or MLA + Inkling (global)"}} MIX --> SCA["ShortConv (MLA layers only)"] --> PA(["partial = attn out"]) PA --> GM["AttnRes gate
history + partial"] Hin --> GM GM --> M1["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] --> MOE{{"LatentMoE + 2 shared experts"}} MOE --> SCM["ShortConv"] --> PB(["block b_i = attn out + MoE out"]) PB --> Hout[("appended to history")] ``` **3a. Kimi Delta Attention, the local mixer (layers 0, 1, 2, 4 at d512; D = 512, 4 heads × 128).** ```mermaid flowchart TB kx["x"] --> kq["q = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_q))"] & kk["k = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_k))"] & kv["v = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_v))"] kx --> kg["decay g = −5 · σ(exp(A_log) · (x W_a↓ W_a↑ + dt_bias))
rank-128 gate, per channel; A_log per head"] kx --> kb["write strength β = σ(x W_β), per head"] kq & kk --> kn["L2-norm q, k; q × 1/√128"] kn & kv & kg & kb --> rec["delta rule, chunked Pallas kernels (chunk 16)
S_t = (I − β k kᵀ) Diag(e^g) S_{t−1} + β k vᵀ
o_t = S_tᵀ q_t · state resets at document starts"] rec --> kon["per-head RMSNorm (shared 128-wide scale)"] --> kog["× σ(x W_g), per channel"] --> ko["W_o → sublayer out
no RoPE, no window, no output ShortConv"] ``` **3b. MLA + Inkling, the global mixer (layers 3 and 5 at d512).** ```mermaid flowchart TB mx["x"] --> mq["q = x W_q (full rank, 4 × 128)"] mx --> ml["KV latent = RMSNorm(x W_dkv), 512 wide, learnable gain"] --> mk["k = latent W_uk"] & mv["v = latent W_uv"] mx --> rel["Inkling bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]
R = x W_r (16 per head) · P 16 × 1024, shared across heads"] mq & mk & mv & rel --> fa["FA4 causal attention (fwd + SM90 bwd)
logits × 1/√128 (qk_mult 1) · no RoPE · no QK-norm
Inkling bias added before softmax"] fa --> xsa["XSA: subtract each head's component along its own v"] --> mg["× 2σ(x W_gate), per head, zero-init"] --> mo["W_o → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` **3c. LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing (every layer).** ```mermaid flowchart TB ex["x (512)"] --> fused["one fused GEMM:
router · W_latent↓ · shared-expert gate/up"] fused --> rt["router logits (fp32)
top-(8+1) on logit − β_QB; 9th = threshold α"] rt --> qb["QB: β_e = global (1 − 8/384) quantile of logit − α
10k-bin histogram each step; router bias = −β, not trained"] rt --> cw["combine weights = σ(unbiased logits) of the top 8,
renormalized to sum to 2.5"] fused --> lat["latent = RMSNorm(x W_latent↓), 256 wide"] lat & cw --> ep["384 SwiGLU experts, hidden 256
pooled-wave EP all-to-all over 8 GPUs, capacity 1.15"] ep --> up["W_latent↑ 256 → 512"] fused --> sh["2 shared SwiGLU experts, 512 → 256 → 512
down projections fused into one GEMM"] up & sh --> sum["routed + shared → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` ¹ AttnRes rolls a new block at layer *i* while `i % max(1, L // 8) == 0` and fewer than 8 blocks exist. At d512 and d768 every layer closes a block. At d1024 (12 layers) and d1280 (14 layers) only layers 0–7 do, so layers 8 and up all accumulate into one running partial instead of their own blocks. **Optimizer routing:** - **MuonH:** every attention and MoE matrix, and every GatedNorm (KDA `W_β` at 2× the MuonH LR). - **AdamH:** lm_head. - **Adam:** embedding, router, attention output gate, norm gains, ShortConv kernels, KDA decay parameters, Inkling weights. - **Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR:** the AttnRes queries. ## Baseline: clean KMA Branch [`fasttrack-moe-kma`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/fasttrack-moe-kma) @ `4eba59cafa`. Build from this branch. The recipe below covers every model and optimizer component. Values are for d512 unless noted; the code is `experiments/grug/fast_track/{model,optimizer,heuristic,launch}.py`. **Shape** | Rung | Width D | Layers | Local (KDA) / global (MLA) layers | Heads × head dim | Batch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | d512 | 512 | 6 | 4 / 2 | 4 × 128 | 128 | | d768 | 768 | 8 | 6 / 2 | 6 × 128 | 128 | | d1024 | 1024 | 12 | 9 / 3 | 8 × 128 | 256 | | d1280 | 1280 | 14 | 10 / 4 | 10 × 128 | 256 | - Every 4th layer and the last layer are global; all other layers are local. - The run uses a 16k vocab and sequence length 4096 with packed documents. Every ShortConv and the KDA state respect document boundaries (the KDA state resets at each document start). - Weights are initialized with std 0.5/√D. Compute is bf16. **Embedding and output** - Token embedding → RMSNorm → GatedNorm. The result is AttnRes source 0. - Output path: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → untied lm_head (`output_proj`). - The fused lm_head + cross-entropy loop uses a vocab tile of 8192. - GatedNorm (every GatedNorm in the model) is `x · sigmoid(W_up · SiLU(W_down · x))`, with a rank-128 bottleneck. **Block (every layer)** - **Attention sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → mixer (KDA or MLA). - **MoE sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → MoE → ShortConv on the MoE output. - Each ShortConv is a 4-tap causal depthwise conv. **Local layers: Kimi Delta Attention** (Kimi K3's layer) - **Projections:** q/k/v are D → N·128 with full heads (no GQA). Each goes through a ShortConv followed by SiLU. q and k are L2-normalized, and q is scaled by 1/√128. - **Decay:** per-channel log-decay `g = −5·sigmoid(exp(A_log)·(x·W_a_down·W_a_up + dt_bias))`. - The gate projection has rank 128. - `A_log` is one value per head, initialized to 0. - `dt_bias` is one value per channel, initialized so the decay rate spans 0.02–0.5. - **Write strength:** `β = sigmoid(x·W_β)`, one value per head. - **Recurrence:** `S_t = (I − β·k·kᵀ)·Diag(exp(g))·S_{t−1} + β·k·vᵀ`, read out as `o_t = S_tᵀ·q_t`. - It runs as chunked Pallas kernels, with a stable block-doubling inverse inside each chunk. - **Output:** per-head RMSNorm with a learnable 128-wide scale shared across heads → full-rank per-channel gate `sigmoid(x·W_g)` → `W_o`. - No positional encoding, no window, no XSA, and no ShortConv on the branch output. **Global layers: MLA + Inkling relative position** - **q:** full-rank, D → N·128 (no Q latent). - **k and v:** k = `W_uk · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)` and v = `W_uv · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)`. - They share one 512-wide KV latent, with a learnable RMSNorm on the latent. - Heads are 128 wide with no RoPE part. - There's no ShortConv on K, so the up-projections can be absorbed at inference. - **Scaling:** no QK-norm; `qk_mult` = 1, i.e. standard 1/√128 logit scaling. - **Position — Inkling relative-position bias**, added to the pre-softmax logits in place of RoPE: - `bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]`, where `R = x·W_r` is 16 values per head. - `P` is a bank of shape [16 × 1024] shared across heads. The relative extent is 1024. - It runs inside the FA4 attention kernel (forward, backward, and the SM90 backward pass). - **XSA** (exclusive self-attention): subtract the component of each head's output that is parallel to its own value vector. - **Output gate:** per head, `2·sigmoid(x·W_gate)`. `W_gate` is zero-initialized, so the gate is 1 at init. - The branch output also gets a ShortConv. **MoE sublayer (LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing)** - **Experts:** 384 routed experts, top-8. Each is a SwiGLU with hidden size D/2. - **Latent space:** experts operate in a D/2-wide latent. The input goes through `W_latent_down` → RMSNorm, and the combined expert output goes back up through `W_latent_up`. - **Router:** reads the full-width token and computes logits in fp32. - Experts are selected by top-(8+1) on bias-adjusted logits, where the 9th logit is the threshold α. - Combine weights are the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, renormalized to sum to 2.5. - **Quantile balancing:** each step, each expert's threshold β is the global (1 − K/E) quantile of the logit margins (logit − α), read from a 10k-bin histogram. The router bias is set to −β. - The router bias is not trained by gradient. - **Capacity:** capacity factor 1.15, with pooled-wave expert-parallel dispatch. Receiver ranks are sort-based and the expand backward is gather-based. - **Shared experts:** 2 shared SwiGLU experts that bypass the latent: D → D/2 hidden → D. - **Fused projections:** - The router, latent-down, and both shared experts' gate/up projections run as one GEMM. - The shared experts' down-projections run as one GEMM. **Residual stream: Block Attention Residuals** - **Sources:** the embedding source, one running sum per completed block of sublayer outputs, and the running partial sum of the current block. - The model has 8 blocks. Block sums use the raw sublayer outputs. - **Gates:** every sublayer (attention and MoE) has its own gate, and there is one final gate before the output norm. Each gate has one learned pseudo-query `q ∈ ℝᴰ`, zero-initialized so every gate starts as a uniform average. - **Mixing:** per token, `logitᵢ = q · rms_norm(sourceᵢ)`, using a parameter-free (frozen) RMS key norm, then `softmax` over sources and a weighted sum of the raw sources. - **Implementation:** - Each completed block is scored once against every gate that reads it. - Backward: at d512 the layer's forward intermediates are saved. At d768–d1280 each layer is recomputed. At d1280 the attention branch is also rematerialized. - The model keeps one layer stack per mixer kind. **Optimizer** | Group | Update rule | LR | Parameters | |---|---|---|---| | `muonh` | MuonH | MuonH LR | all attention and MoE matrices: MLA `W_q`/`W_dkv`/`W_uk`/`W_uv`/`W_o`; KDA `W_q`/`W_k`/`W_v`/`W_o`/`W_g`; experts; shared experts; latent down/up. Also every GatedNorm `W_down`/`W_up`. | | `kda_beta` | MuonH | 2 × MuonH LR | KDA `W_β` | | `adamh` | AdamH | MuonH LR | lm_head (`output_proj`) | | `adam` | Adam | Adam LR | token embedding; router; attention output gate; router bias slot (overwritten by QB); all 1-D norm gains; ShortConv kernels; KDA `W_a_down`/`W_a_up`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`; Inkling `W_r` and `P` | | `attn_res_query` | Adam | 0.1 × Adam LR | the AttnRes pseudo-queries | - **MuonH:** Nesterov momentum 0.95 → Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (5 quintic steps, bucketed across same-shape matrices) → a step along that direction, then projection back onto the matrix's Frobenius sphere. Each matrix's norm stays fixed at its init value. - **AdamH:** the Adam direction with the same Frobenius-sphere (hyperball) projection. - **Adam:** β1 0.9. Only the router and the attention output gate get decoupled weight decay (0.02). No other parameter gets weight decay, and there's no gradient clipping. - **Schedule:** 1% warmup, then linear decay to 0.05× peak. - **Peak values** from `MoeHeuristic` (they depend on tokens, width and batch): - Adam LR = `0.0876 · tokens^−0.346 · D^−0.345 · √(tokens per batch)`. - MuonH LR = 13/3 × Adam LR. - β2 = `0.999^(tokens per batch / 131072)`. - ε = `9.68e−18 · √(steps)`. - At d512 with 2384 steps: MuonH LR 0.0227, Adam LR 0.0052, β2 0.996, ε 4.7e−16. Submit at **batch** priority (the launcher's default is interactive, so pass it): ``` NO_PROXY="*" uv run python -m experiments.grug.fast_track.launch --submit \ --target-cluster cw-us-east-02a --priority batch \ --run-id --size d512 --recipe kma --num-steps <8-min steps> --version ``` ## Compute - cw-us-east-02a at **batch** priority. - **At most 10 active runs at once**, probes included. - **Limit runs above d768** to keep the experimentation rate high. d1024 and d1280 runs take hours and hold a slot the whole time, so save them for changes that have already passed gate 1 or that need extra scales because of curve-fitting risk. - Don't save checkpoints (the launcher default). ## For humans Comment with a research direction for the agent, such as "try X" or "combine A and B". The agent picks up new comments at its next batch. An experiment can still be useful when a parameter change causes the loss to diverge: the result shows the system’s sensitivity to that parameter. ## For the agent - Read `experiments/grug/fast_track/README.md` and `agent.md` first. Where they differ from this issue, this issue wins; the main difference is the fixed-time objective. - Run 5–10 experiments per batch, and prioritize human comments when picking the next one. - Ask for clarification in the thread if helpful, but never hold a batch waiting for an answer: state your assumption and correct it in the next batch. - Start at d512. When a change beats the current best by more than 0.005, validate it at d768. - Post **one comment per batch** and edit it as runs finish. Start it with 🤖 and include: - the batch goal, and which human comments it addresses; - a table with one row per run: change | branch@commit | W&B link | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ vs current best; - a 1–3 line takeaway and the planned next batch. - **Branches:** prefix with `ladderclimb_v1_`, and link the exact commit each job ran. - **W&B:** project `marin_moe`, with short prefixed run IDs such as `lc1-b03-…` (names over 128 characters fail at init). - Add the `agent-generated` label to any issue or PR you open. - Keep the **Status** table below updated with a concise chronology of improvements. ## Studies Deep dives and multi-batch studies, newest first. topics.title: Marin Belay Intake
topics.body:
🤖 **Marin Belay Intake: post research suggestions for [Marin Belay v1 (#9451)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451) here.**

Marin Belay is an agent-run experiment loop that hill-climbs the grug `fast_track` scaling ladder (Paloma macro loss, fixed 8-minute 8×H100 budget). The agent reads and acts only on the main thread (#9451), which is limited to users with write access. Suggestions from anyone else come in through this issue:

1. **Post your suggestion as a comment here.** One idea per comment, with a paper link or a short rationale if you have one.
2. **A maintainer reviews it.** When a member of the `marin-devs` team reacts with 👍, an automated workflow (every ~5 minutes) copies the comment verbatim into #9451, attributed to you and linked back here.
3. **The workflow then adds 🚀 to your comment**, meaning it has been transferred. It transfers each comment once; editing a comment after the 🚀 does not re-send it.

Suggestions that are off-topic, duplicate existing work, or ask the agent to do anything other than ML research on the ladder won't be approved. The main thread's Status section lists what has been tried and the current best recipe.

topics.title: [eval] Check in the September evaluation campaign
topics.body:
Check in the model, evaluator, and launcher configurations for the September 2026 evaluation campaign, together with the runtime fixes needed for serving, retry, resume, and coverage. The launcher validates external pins, writes immutable effective-config snapshots, and accepts an optional submitter-controlled version label. That label does not attest policy conformance.

Harbor results are bound to the full model and hosted judge configurations, dataset, policy, runtime, and task limit. Resume checks this identity before submission and reuse. A changed checkpoint under the same served name is rejected, as are existing roots without model-bound provenance. Recovery retries known infrastructure failures and unscored trials while retaining scored outcomes and unknown errors.

The frozen Harbor runtime pins 94b118022fe3e677784a638daf33d57a836fa5fe and includes the Tau3 adapter. The Evalchemy lock and generated pin match Marin's external dependency configuration.

SWE-bench uses the native Mini-SWE adapter from merged [Harbor #232](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/232) and [#233](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/233). Its 32,768-token context includes the prompt and reply together. Mini-SWE counts the rendered prompt through the serving tokenizer, including tools and the generation prefix, and caps the reply within the remaining budget and server window. Harbor loads Mini-SWE's base configuration before applying overrides and selects its batch agent, which saves the trajectory on context exhaustion without prompting. Harbor can then verify the existing patch.

Sotopia uses the packaged agent from merged [Harbor #231](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/231). Judge failures become verifier infrastructure errors. The Marin agent wrappers and their harness dependencies are removed. Sotopia's native generation still does not enforce its declared context budget, so those results cannot establish conformance to the 32K context policy.

Part of #9566.

topics.title: Experiment: Hero throughput and expert drops at 8K and 16K context
topics.body:
Agent-driven experiment issue: the runs and this record were produced by a Claude agent, supervised by @mcwitt.

## TL;DR

On one GB200 NVL72 rack, restoring the hero's step-180000 checkpoint at a fixed 4.19M tokens per step, 8K context trains at 297.0k tokens/s, 1.6% below 4K, and 16K at 292.5k tokens/s, 3.1% below 4K. The fraction of expert assignments dropped rises from 1.9e-4 at 4K to 8.3e-4 at 8K (4.5×) and 2.9e-3 at 16K (16×). The drops come from the receiving shard's per-chunk capacity; the ragged transport counts all of them as `sender_dropped` (see the correction comment). Each arm has three seeds; the seed-to-seed standard deviation is at most 0.03 MFU points and 4% to 7% of the drop fraction.

## Description

The hero plan in #8435 moves from 4K to 8K sequences at 50% of training (step ~195k) and to 65K at ~95%. These runs measure what the 8K switch costs in throughput and expert-capacity drops before it happens, with 16K as the next point and a 4K control from the same checkpoint.

Setup:

* Source: `main` at f38da1173de79f1eacd5f54bcfb88db6cb0a9f6e with no code changes. Launcher: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_diagnostics.py`.
* Checkpoint: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-180000`, the newest permanent hero checkpoint on 2026-09-30. The current hero run id records that it started from step 146k.
* Hardware and parallelism: one rack (16 nodes × 4 GB200), EP64, the hero's ragged all-to-all transport and capacity factor 1.15.
* Every arm keeps 4,194,304 tokens per step (65,536 per GPU), so the learning rate from the hero's heuristic (`MoeHeuristic` in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/heuristic.py`, which scales with tokens per step and total tokens) is the same in all arms. `--schedule-steps 390251` is the hero's full schedule length, so the restored step sits at the hero's position in the learning-rate schedule.
* `qk_mult`, the multiplier on the query-key attention scale, follows the #8435 extension rule `1.3 × (0.1 × ln(seq / 4096) + 1)`.
* Each run trains steps 180000 to 180099 with the production watch interval (10) and coordinated GC interval (100). There is no eval and no checkpoint write.
* The trainer seed sets the data shuffle, so seeds 0, 1, and 2 train on different batches.
* Statistics cover steps 180010 to 180099 (90 steps). Each run contributes its median MFU, median tokens/s, and mean drop fraction; the tables report mean ± standard deviation across the three seeds. Starting the window at step 180030 instead moves no run's median MFU by more than 0.03 points.

| Arm | `--seq-len` | `--batch-size` | `--qk-mult` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4K control | 4096 | 1024 | 1.3 |
| 8K | 8192 | 512 | 1.39 |
| 16K | 16384 | 256 | 1.48 |

Command for one run (8K, seed 0):

```bash
python -m experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.launch_diagnostics \
  --run-id mhep-ctx8k-s0-20260930 --seed 0 \
  --num-steps 180100 --schedule-steps 390251 \
  --batch-size 512 --seq-len 8192 --qk-mult 1.39 --gc-interval 100 \
  --restore-from s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-180000 \
  --version dev --run
```

## Results

| Arm | tokens/s | vs 4K | step time | MFU | drop fraction | vs 4K |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4K | 301.9k ± 0.2k | | 13.89 s | 28.25 ± 0.02% | 1.86e-4 ± 0.08e-4 | 1× |
| 8K | 297.0k ± 0.2k | −1.6% | 14.12 s | 28.47 ± 0.02% | 8.29e-4 ± 0.39e-4 | 4.5× |
| 16K | 292.5k ± 0.3k | −3.1% | 14.34 s | 29.37 ± 0.03% | 2.94e-3 ± 0.20e-3 | 16× |

The logged `moe/receiver_drop_fraction` is zero in every run because the ragged transport hard-codes it to zero and counts receiver-capacity clipping as `sender_dropped`. Peak HBM was 103.1 GiB per GPU in every run. In every run, including the 4K control, the mean drop fraction over steps 180055 to 180099 was 0.75 to 1.00 times the mean over steps 180010 to 180054, so part of the measured drop fraction may be a transient after restore.

The live hero (11 racks, 4K) measured over steps 183310 to 183710 on 2026-09-30 had a median MFU of 26.47% and a mean drop fraction of 9.1e-5.

Caveats:

* MFU uses the analytic FLOP count, which charges more attention FLOPs per token at longer sequences (full causal attention on every fourth layer, a 2048-token window elsewhere). MFU therefore rises with sequence length while tokens/s falls. Compare arms by tokens/s.
* The one-rack 4K drop fraction is about 2× the 11-rack hero's. We have not tested the cause. The ratios between arms are the quantity to carry to the hero; an 8K hero drop fraction near 4e-4 is an extrapolation from that ratio, not a measurement.
* Each run covers 100 steps after the switch. Routing over thousands of steps at the new length is untested.
* The 8K and 16K arms change `qk_mult` together with sequence length.
* The diagnostic's peak learning rate comes from a one-rack token budget and is 0.69× the hero's. The diagnostic also leaves the attn_gate/router weight decay at 0 (the hero uses 0.02). Loss values are not comparable with the hero's.
* At 8K and 16K, XLA logged at compile time that rematerialization could only reduce its memory estimate to 193 GiB against a 161 GiB limit. The warning does not stop compilation. The runs trained normally with a runtime peak HBM of 103.1 GiB, the same as 4K, so the estimate overstated actual use.

## Links

* W&B runs (project `marin_moe`, group `moe-hero-ep`): 4K [s0](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx4k-s0-20260930), [s1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx4k-s1-20260930), [s2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx4k-s2-20260930); 8K [s0](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx8k-s0-20260930), [s1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx8k-s1-20260930), [s2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx8k-s2-20260930); 16K [s0](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx16k-s0-20260930), [s1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx16k-s1-20260930), [s2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx16k-s2-20260930)
* Hero plan: #8435. 262K context-parallel probe on the same hardware: #8754.

## Conclusion

At the planned 4K to 8K switch, expect about 1.6% fewer tokens per second and about 4.5× the 4K drop fraction, still below 0.1% of assignments on one rack. At 16K the costs are 3.1% and 16×.

topics.title: [grafana] Announce hero retries during restore
topics.body:
Announce Iris retry events while a replacement hero attempt is initializing or has not published phase telemetry. Previously, the training-phase gate cleared Grafana's five-minute pending alert when a new attempt began restoring. The retry event then aged out after 15 minutes before training resumed.

Keep the signal-based health checks gated on training. The [September 30 incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/568) exposed this gap.

topics.title: Complete batches across prefill and slot limits
topics.body:
Complete batches when prompts span configured prefill buffers or the available
sequence slots are full. Admit pending requests as finished sequences release
slots and KV pages while preserving request and generation order.

The loop continues until every request finishes, bounded by the configured
context length, and raises if requests remain but a decode iteration produces no
tokens. Focused CPU coverage in the [engine tests](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9650/files)
exercises repeated batches, cloned generations, and decode rounds larger than
the context. Accelerator performance remains unmeasured.
topics.head: 9d85d5737b5e4cb74445f2678bb648552724338e

topics.title: Add paged attention serving plumbing
topics.body:
Add array-first paged attention for mixed prefill and decode. The reference
path streams interleaved KV-cache pages with absolute-position causal masking,
sliding windows, soft caps, and explicit KV-head sharding. The public entry
point dispatches between the reference and existing TPU ragged implementations.

Focused [paged-attention tests](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9652/files)
cover mixed requests, page metadata, head grouping, and reference dispatch.
Full-model serving parity and end-to-end accelerator performance remain
unmeasured. Builds on [#9658](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9658).
topics.head: 27999a314b553d2cae643823081a3c81ee8d60fe

topics.title: Reconcile Snowball prefill and decode
topics.body:
Run Snowball prefill and decode over paged KV caches while preserving the
model's existing attention, gating, and MoE behavior. Packed requests use
absolute positions, padded tokens do not route, and expert-parallel decode
retains every routed assignment.

The loader accepts packed expert banks and per-expert projection tensors used by
the existing exports. The [Snowball tests](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9653/files)
compare chunked mixed-request decode with full forward. Accelerator throughput
and production checkpoint decoding remain unmeasured. Builds on
[#9652](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9652).

topics.title: Sample logits from explicitly sharded models
topics.body:
Select sampled token rows and replicate those rows across the vocabulary axis
before vocabulary-wide sampling. This lets Grug-style models generate through
the inference engine without gathering every prefill token's sharded logits.

The engine test in the [stacked diff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9654/files)
covers explicit output sharding and the combined sampling path.
An additional tiny BF16 Snowball smoke run completed on CPU; accelerator
decoder throughput remains unmeasured. Builds on
[#9650](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9650).
topics.head: d4f153d3bc8cceea9a5403cb1cf777747d74d913

topics.title: Preserve paged short-convolution history
topics.body:
Preserve causal short-convolution inputs across paged prefill and decode. Each
physical page stores the last `kernel_size - 1` activation rows, page cloning
copies that history, and padded tokens cannot overwrite it.

CPU FP32/BF16 parity tests in the [short-convolution diff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9655/files)
cover mixed requests, page crossings, clone divergence, and reset against the
full-sequence reference. The cache is not yet wired into the Hero inference
model, and accelerator performance remains unmeasured. Builds on
[#9653](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9653).
topics.head: eeae24a841ae39b79a8cfbb3768db7f09b6e0918

topics.title: [levanter] Add opt-in GPU paged decode with sliding windows
topics.body:
Add opt-in GPU paged decode over the existing interleaved KV cache, with causal positions and sliding windows. Mixed and prefill batches use the reference implementation. Existing model configs can select `gpu_pallas_bf16_3x`; backend defaults remain unchanged. Builds on #9652.

The initial FP32 IEEE attention-value dot regressed at Hero batch 8. Reconstructing its FP32 probabilities as three BF16 components permits tensor-core dots while retaining FP32 accumulation. For local Hero attention (batch 8, context 4096, window 2048, 12 KV heads, 4 query groups, head dimension 128, pages 128, 8 splits), H100 median host latency falls from 2,140 to 162 microseconds and summed CUPTI kernel time from 2,011 to 57.1. GB200 falls from 1,637 to 183 microseconds host and 1,474 to 43.7 on device. Twenty repeated calls exclude compilation, cache updates, and model work. Sixteen splits did not improve this workload.

All eight small GPU parity cases pass on both devices (integration aca7d8ec6c). The full-shape reference comparison passes local batch 1 and global batches 1/8; local batch 8 differs from the FP32 reference at 3 of 49,152 elements beyond atol=rtol=1e-4 on each GPU (maximum difference 0.00024414). A float64 oracle agrees with the candidate at all four investigated coordinates: the reference rounded three incorrectly, and the IEEE split-K path rounded the fourth incorrectly. The independent full-output float64 regression, using direct nearest-even BF16 rounding, passes all 49,152 outputs on both H100 and GB200, alongside all eight small cases (12.57 and 11.28 seconds). The candidate remains opt-in. FlashInfer XQA on the same arrays measures 35–67 microseconds host on H100 and 46–62 on GB200 across these shapes, with different output rounding. No full-model vLLM speed parity is established.

The benchmark reports compilation, synchronized host latency, optional CUPTI per-kernel or TPU XPlane module durations, full-output errors, and matched FlashInfer or pinned TPU-vLLM RPA comparisons. The default TPU RPA baseline ran successfully (181.5 microseconds versus 748.1 for reference on local batch 1, maximum output difference 0.00097656). Matching query/output packing enables its FP32 mode: 183.5 microseconds, maximum difference 0.00048828. These deviations are against the FP32 reference; a full float64 oracle check of those baselines is pending.

Removing query-padding launches and combining split outputs in one Pallas kernel preserves all eight small hardware parity cases. H100 measures 148 microseconds host / 53.2 on device; GB200 measures 216 / 39.7, so device time improves while host timing remains variable. The combined stack passes 33 focused cases with 37 accelerator skips. The inherited TPU precision port passes 56 strict cases with 9 GPU skips on each of v4, v5p and v6e, including the corrected full-output FP64 oracle and both DMA modes. Its v5p median host latency at batch sizes 1/8 is 359/1886 microseconds versus 748/3059 for reference; XPlane module time is 242/1747 versus 626/2935. Tiny BF16 Snowball and Hero EP2 generation also completes on v4/v6e. Retaining arithmetic residuals roughly doubles TPU latency relative to the earlier candidate that failed the full-output oracle. All numerical tolerances are unchanged.

The earlier float64-oracle passes used NumPy’s FP64-to-BF16 cast, which can double-round through FP32 near BF16 midpoints. The oracle now quantizes FP64 directly to nearest-even BF16; exhaustive midpoint and boundary tests cover the correction. GPU arithmetic is unchanged. The corrected nine-case gate passes on both GPUs in `grug-h100-direct-bf16-oracle-20261002` and `grug-gb200-direct-bf16-oracle-20261002`.

On the same TPU source/runtime, two DMA buffers reduce batch-8 device time from 1635 to 1161 microseconds (host 1769 to 1312), with identical numerical comparisons. Pinned vLLM RPA takes 277 microseconds on device for the same workload but has different output rounding. The one-buffer default remains unchanged. The benchmark emitted all thirteen expected rows; the initial compiler archive exceeded its size limit, and a subsequent bounded capture preserved 44.57 MiB of XPlane and schedule evidence.

The inherited TPU update replaces general division by a power-of-two scale with exact inverse-scale multiplication. The v5p strict gate passes 59 cases with 9 GPU skips. A same-process, identical-input comparison reduces batch-8 device time with two DMA buffers from 1245 to 1015 microseconds with bit-identical outputs; it measures the local attention entry point, excluding public-wrapper metadata.

The inherited component-packing candidate preserves all 65,280 finite BF16 bit patterns in CPU tests and passes the affected suite. Its accelerator parity and timing remain pending in #9652.

topics.title: [grug] Add hero launch controls for a context-length switch
topics.body:
The scaling-ladder launcher holds 4,194,304 tokens per rack per update, so the sequence batch shrinks as the context grows (2816 sequences at 16K on 11 racks). The step count (390251), learning rates, decay, and gate/router weight decay therefore match the 4K run. The hero's context length, QK multipliers, and capacity factor live in HERO_MODEL. --qk-mult and --qk-mult-long-scale (global layers only) override the QK multipliers for trial arms and ladder rungs; trial arms set the context length on their branch alongside the history. Eval packs at the training context, as on main, so the eval_dropless/* series shift at each switch. For short trial arms, --eval-every overrides the eval cadence.

The hero's context history is checked in, like the data mix's switch point: HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES in launch_scaling_ladder.py lists each context the d6144 hero trained at before its current one with the step it ended at, and HERO_FLOPS_BASELINE_TOTAL holds the parent's cumulative training FLOPs at the last switch. A context-switch deploy PR edits Python only: it sets the HERO_MODEL fields, appends one entry to HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES, and sets HERO_FLOPS_BASELINE_TOTAL, so a second switch (4K to 16K, then 16K to 64K) is described exactly and trigger_hero.sh is unchanged. The launcher turns the history into a FlopsBaseline at the last end step and, through the prior_context_phases argument of harrier_mix_2026_08_18_data_config, into LmDataConfig.prior_context_phases, with each earlier phase's Harrier stage schedule and shuffle blocks at its own batch size, so the Harrier sources continue from their earlier reads. At d6144 the launcher rejects a history that does not start at 4K, repeats a length between adjacent phases (including the current context), or disagrees with whether the baseline is set. LmDataConfig rejects end steps that do not increase, and rejects any switch below the 1e23-FLOP simulated-epoching cutoff because the data offsets assume each source reads its whole cache. The narrow rungs take no history.

The live run is unchanged: trigger_hero.sh is identical to main and launches the 4K HERO_MODEL with no FLOPs baseline. A switch still needs a GPU rehearsal from the handoff checkpoint and agreed trial thresholds; see the inventory and validation plan in #9615.

Part of #9615

topics.title: Pod creation fails on a node with 65K empty Silo cgroups
topics.body:
On October 2, new pods failed to start on CoreWeave node `g5bc6da`, blocking new jobs. Kubernetes reported `no space left on device` while creating a pod’s cgroup, the kernel group used to track and limit container resources. The node still reported healthy, and its filesystem had 3.55 TB free.

The host cgroup tree had 65,535 descendant groups. Of these, 65,412 were under `/silo`; that entire subtree contained no processes. This strongly suggests exhaustion of the kernel’s roughly 64K memory-cgroup ID space, though we have not traced the failing allocator.

Silo is the nested container runtime running inside our privileged Iris job `muchanem.cap-pipeline-host-53`. Two sampled container IDs from its `containerd-shim` processes matched empty `/silo` cgroups. This points to a cleanup problem in that workload’s runtime, but we have not identified the code path responsible. We have no evidence that CoreWeave’s host containerd created these groups.

Please investigate whether completed containers leave cgroups and shim processes behind, and fix the cleanup path. Verify that repeated container creation and teardown do not keep increasing either count. Coordinate cleanup of the affected node with the pipeline owner; an empty cgroup alone does not establish that it is safe to remove while the runtime is active.

---

topics.title: Share Hero and Snowball checkpoint export mechanics
topics.body:
Share bounded HF shard-writing code between Hero and the Levanter converter used by Snowball. Hero reuses the converter's 5 GB file planner; a source tensor larger than that target remains whole. Local files are written directly, while remote files stage under `TMPDIR` before upload.

All JAX ranks replicate tensors in matching order. Only process zero copies weights to CPU and writes files. One writer process supports host-local paths and existing HF upload callbacks. An `ExitStack` owns each memory reservation during gathering; successful submission transfers cleanup to the shard-write task's completion callback. Process zero broadcasts writer failures at matching checks on all ranks.

Hero resume verifies the export request identity and shard checksums before reuse. It writes `export-manifest.json` after all shards and HF metadata to mark completion.

CPU export checks cover exact Hero/Snowball weights, concurrent uploads and two-rank failure/recovery. Full-size accelerator exports and live cloud/HF uploads remain untested.

topics.body:

Operator cordons remain. Running tasks are not evicted.

Health and cordon evidence remain in node annotations when Finelog is unavailable. Configuration, scratch-object lifecycle, and recovery are documented in the CoreWeave guide. topics.title: [experiment] Snowball SFT on GLM-5.3 traces from Skill2Env biology tasks
topics.body:
## TL;DR

**Experiment finished on October 9, 2026.** Closing with no demonstrated improvement on the primary Pi/BixBench evaluation. The remaining uncertainties are recorded as limitations; no further training, evaluation, or investigation is planned under this issue.

The biology-only SFT run is complete, but the primary evaluation on **Pi**, the harness used to collect the teacher traces and intended for deployment, has not demonstrated improved BixBench performance. On five questions selected using historical runtime, **Pi with thinking enabled scored parent 1/5 versus SFT 0/5**, with all attempts graded. The final response contained an unexecuted tool call in the parsed reasoning field in 1/5 parent attempts and 5/5 SFT attempts. The affected parent attempt had already written the correct answer and still received credit. Two SFT attempts executed no tools, while three executed tools before that ending. This failure therefore also exists in the parent; it was observed more often after SFT in this small sample. With thinking disabled, the parent scored 1/5; SFT had one correct and one incorrect graded attempt plus three verifier timeouts. Those missing grades prevent a complete accuracy comparison and are not counted as zero. This is a small diagnostic sample, not a full BixBench result. See the [primary Pi results and matched controls](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6069563534).

The run used the September 21 Datakit parent, biology traces only, three epochs, peak LR 1e-4, 128k sequences, effective batch 16, and a final-only checkpoint. The dataset contains 5,120 reconstructed windows and 73,894,261 assistant target tokens per epoch from 1,319 attempts across 264 tasks, without reward/completion filtering or replay data. The [published-input audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6069710545) found no supervised tool tags inside open reasoning; the cause of the observed Pi behavior remains unresolved.

Terminus-2 and the synthetic tasks are **secondary diagnostics** of format adherence and transfer to other harnesses. Terminus scored parent 1/5 versus SFT 0/5 on the same real questions; this is not the primary measure of the Pi-trained model. The [Terminus trace analysis](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083049902) and [completed prompt ablation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083809697) investigate format sensitivity. The latter accepted 36/36 parent versus 0/36 SFT first responses under the Terminus schema; this remains a secondary format-transfer diagnostic. A Terminus-specific workaround would not establish a fix for Pi.

## Description

Use the existing [Skill2Env Harbor release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env) to collect GLM-5.3 demonstrations for Snowball. This issue owns task selection, rollout collection, SFT, and the before/after experiment. [#9630](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9630) owns Skill2Env Atlas intake; [#9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258) owns biology evaluation coverage and protocols.

Start with biology tasks, prioritizing biological data analysis relevant to BixBench. If the usable pool is too small, consider a separately recorded expansion to general scientific data analysis and statistics. Keep relay methods, where a teacher takes over from student-generated actions, for a later experiment.

### Candidate data

The October 5 metadata inspection covered all 7,496 tasks in release revision 2, version `1.0.1`, with content digest `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. The 268 candidates are a source-skill and description-based shortlist, not an exhaustive taxonomy or a validated training pool.

| Candidate category | Tasks | Source-skill identifiers |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Genomics and single-cell analysis | 95 | 40 |
| Proteins and structure | 49 | 16 |
| Chemistry and drug discovery | 45 | 22 |
| Biomedical data and lab workflows | 79 | 28 |
| Total | 268 | 106 |

Examples include paired airway RNA-seq analysis with PyDESeq2, sparse CELLxGENE summaries, Scanpy PBMC QC and clustering, DepMap dependency analysis, and pysam BAM/VCF processing. Different skill identifiers can cover related workflows; 106 identifiers do not establish 106 independent task families. Many released tasks repair pipelines against offline fixtures. Their usefulness for BixBench remains a hypothesis.

Skill2Env's [source attribution table](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env/blob/507eab4d9952968de2be98f8729d3c66d487285a/SkillHub/skillhub_source_licenses.csv) includes K-Dense scientific skills and AlterLab academic skills. Preserve task-specific source and license records when selecting data or sharing traces. The selection rule below preserves this initial shortlist independently of temporary local files.

### Pilot sequence

1. Review candidate instructions, environments, and graders. Six initial tasks passed reference/no-op controls. The user authorized direct collection on the other 262 metadata-selected candidates; those tasks have not passed additional controls. Review grader validity when interpreting scores; it is not a selection gate for the unfiltered baseline. Record any grader defects; the existing Atlas assessment found a grader defect in a separate three-task sample.
2. Freeze the task manifest and evaluation split. Group related tasks and shared-data variants when defining development and held-out sets. BixBench-overlap checking is not a prerequisite for this collection, as decided on October 5; preserve task provenance.
3. Pin the Snowball starting checkpoint, tokenizer, training recipe, agent harness, and evaluation settings. Run a small end-to-end collection and formatting check before expanding collection. Record compute budgets before launching sandbox or training work.
4. Generate GLM-5.3 trajectories. The initial collection finished five attempts per task on the six control-checked tasks, for 30 attempted rollouts. The expanded collection targets five attempts for each of the other 262 tasks, for 1,310 new attempts. Preserve every attempt, raw conversations, tool outputs, exact model settings, task revisions, and the full native reward vector; keep incomplete and ungraded outcomes separate. Inspect component-score distributions, solution diversity, and token volume. The first SFT baseline uses all available solver traces without reward or completion filtering. Preserve interrupted prefixes and record conversion or recovery gaps without manufacturing missing content. Rewards are graded; do not reduce them to binary success or require all components to equal 1 by default. Native executable rewards do not reproduce the paper's additional rubric-scoring layer.
5. Prepare all available solver traces for the first SFT baseline; the earlier 200–500 selected-trace target is superseded. Report attempted, complete, graded, and selected traces; component-score distributions; unique tasks and task families; total tokens; and supervised assistant tokens. Size the first SFT run from those observations; the target is a planning budget, not a proven minimum. Prioritize coverage of distinct tasks when expanding collection. Additional attempts on one task do not increase task diversity.
6. Train with loss on assistant turns, preserving user and tool messages as context. Evaluate the final checkpoint against the unchanged Snowball parent on the fixed BixBench protocol using the same Pi harness and budgets. Decide on broader evaluations after reviewing BixBench. Keep infrastructure failures separate from incorrect answers.

Recent Snowball work motivates a bounded test: a [5,000-conversation GLM continuation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9719) regressed on several benchmarks, while [other agent SFT mixtures](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/8669f5b6f97e4e3bae72344a8fd51f4b) improved agent benchmarks. Neither establishes a BixBench benefit from this dataset.

### Agreed SFT settings

| Setting | Selected value |
| --- | --- |
| Parent | `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`; revision `b8c07f7df1df65525abbfdbcd1572318ba11c42f` and native tokenizer/template pinned |
| Data | All available GLM/Pi biology solver traces; no reward or completion filter; no general SFT or pretraining replay |
| Run count and peak LR | One run at `1e-4` |
| Duration | Three epochs |
| Training sequence length | 131,072 tokens; verify actual lengths with the parent tokenizer |
| Effective global batch | 16 sequences per optimizer update; accumulation as needed |
| Parameter updates | Full-parameter SFT; imported router biases frozen, router weights and other model weights trained |
| Optimizer | Fresh AdamH; beta1 0.9, beta2 0.95, epsilon 1e-8, weight decay 0, gradient clipping 1.0 |
| Schedule | 3% warmup, then cosine decay from 1e-4 to 1e-5 over the run |
| Checkpoints | Final model save/export only; no intermediate or per-epoch checkpoints |
| Initial evaluation | Parent and final model on BixBench with identical Pi harness and budgets; broader evaluations deferred until that result |

The nominal batch is 2,097,152 token positions per update, matching 64 × 32,768 in [the teacher-only reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9582). Masking, padding, and sequence construction determine actual supervised tokens. Three epochs and peak LR 1e-4 follow that precedent; its reported evaluations use final checkpoints, and its intermediate checkpoint cadence is undocumented. The final-only saving decision avoids repeated serialization and storage of this model.

Use reconstructed conversations with each actual assistant output supervised once, carried context masked, and interrupted outputs left without invented termination markers. The finalized dataset has 5,120 windows at length 131,072, 320 steps per epoch, and 960 steps total. Target four CoreWeave nodes with eight H100s each. BixBench comparison uses `bixbench-cli-marin-corrections@3` (205 tasks), Pi, one attempt per task, 32,768 context / 8,192 output, and matched grading. The CPU training coordinator is submitted; GPU training remains gated on cache verification.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Unfiltered GLM-5.3 demonstrations of biological analysis improve Snowball's held-out BixBench accuracy under the same harness and execution budget. Measure paired BixBench changes and uncertainty, task coverage, tool-format failures, and response lengths. Broader evaluation is deferred until the BixBench result. Review trace completeness, native grades, and sequence handling before training; preserve negative results.

## Status

The expanded collection completed all 1,310 original task/repetition slots. The final audit proves exactly five attempts per task, with no missing or duplicate pairs. Native reward vectors exist for 1,285 attempts; 25 are ungraded. There are 946 final assistant `stop` markers, 248 output-limit endings, 49 final tool-use stops, eight final error stops, and 59 without an exported final assistant stop reason. Agent timeouts are an overlapping exception class: 86 attempts record one. No verifier-error diagnostic was recorded. Native Pi sessions and ATIF trajectories are present for 1,251 attempts.

Native score patterns across the graded attempts are 574 vectors with every component equal to 1, 381 with mixed or partial component credit, and 330 with every component equal to 0. These remain graded vectors, not binary success labels. The 946 final `stop` markers cover 238 tasks; nine also record runner exceptions, so this marker alone does not establish a clean run. A historical structural screen requiring native session and trajectory, no exception or recorded verifier error, and matched tool calls/replies retains 933 normal candidates. Of those, 558 have every component equal to 1 and cover 161 tasks. Their provider-counted output usage totals 24,112,468 tokens; this includes reasoning and possible auxiliary compaction output and is not a unique Snowball-supervised token count. Four normal traces have unresolved tool-call diagnostics. These screening counts are diagnostic subsets and do not define the unfiltered training pool.

The original batch retained 875 attempts: 829 verified per-attempt archives and 46 [verified fallback recoveries](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6016912375). The continuation executed only the remaining 435 slots and verified all 435 checkpoints, with no further checkpoint failures. It completed at 14:46:11 UTC; cleanup at 14:46:14 reported zero owned sandboxes. The small final Iris archive and completion audit were copied to private durable storage and retrieved for SHA-256 verification. Final archive SHA-256: `4b06bdb9e491145acaddddb0cd44928191386b22b80b3061a3b1a18c5511e68a` (2,240,445 bytes). Original native grades, checkpoint-failure labels, and interrupted-stream diagnostics are preserved.

Both cohorts used native Pi 0.87.0 with 131,072 total context, 32,768 solver output, thinking enabled, native compaction, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, repetition seeds 0–4, and up to 64 concurrent workers. The continuation repaired capture closure and retried a startup that was preempted before teacher generation; it did not rerun attempted slots. Original expanded protocol SHA-256: `24ebb14feb54c3ec97f4c79732a7d42efb2c8cc7c792c2bc6e714dbeb6833997`; continuation: `36e7a611fb25f8e6625934b123ad00f6b33cdace57945b32d7ac5a7ef9852a58`; 262-task manifest: `87f0276f2fe2a3675eb875079363d20d321a80ca216e265539c39a6524f7cd75`. Source archives, notices, launch snapshots, native results, and raw captures are retained.

The six-task control batch is complete: all reference reward components were 1.0 and all no-op components were 0.0, with verifier diagnostics reviewed. The other candidates remain a metadata shortlist. The [seven-attempt Terminus-2 batch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6004311716) is retained separately as diagnostic evidence; its continuation is superseded.

Pi collection completed all 30 planned attempts and retained 29 native reward vectors. Endings: 17 normal, eight output-limited, four agent timeouts, and one ungraded `DaytonaBadGatewayError`. No verifier errors were recorded. The 17 normal traces have matched tool calls and replies, with full or partial native component credit. They cover DepMap, pysam, CELLxGENE, PyDESeq2, and Scanpy; all five scikit-bio attempts ended at an output limit. They contain 869,472 provider-counted output tokens before reward selection and target-tokenizer accounting. No filtering has been applied; the first baseline retains all available solver traces.

Native Pi sessions and ATIF trajectories were retained for 26/30 attempts. Three timeouts lost native log export because `pi.txt` changed during archiving; the infrastructure failure also lacks native agent logs. Raw API captures are retained for all 30 attempts, including three interrupted response streams. The four timeout traces contain repeated identical tool exchanges. The complete archive, source notices, per-file hashes, configuration, launcher, and audit are privately preserved. Archive SHA-256: `61671f943850c0601a9febb3058bf3e1e2df3689b7ef06594280aa89ce087c9f`. No Daytona sandboxes remain.

The teacher uses native Pi 0.87.0, matching the runtime pin in [evaluation policy #9409](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9409), with the [Skill2Env paper, section 3.4](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env/blob/main/paper/Skill2Env_arXiv.pdf) teacher budget: 131,072 total context tokens, a 32,768-token solver output cap, high thinking, and native compaction. Pi's high setting maps to GLM chat-template thinking enabled; no provider `reasoning_effort` tier is sent. BixBench policy instead uses 32,768 total context and 8,192 output tokens; collection and evaluation budgets remain separate. Live requests obeyed the configured cap, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, and repetition seeds 0–4. The largest observed prompt was 98,346 tokens; compaction used a 16,384-token output cap. This is not a full context-boundary stress test.

Execution uses upstream Harbor `bf991e490394ef9c3250a6db2bc5cbda903cb4c3` with a configuration-only adapter around Pi. Native tools, prompt, loop, task resources, and component grades are retained. Setup allows the recorded package mirrors; agent execution allows the scoped model endpoint, and verification retains the task's no-network policy. The initial six-task collection used at most three concurrent trials, native 30-minute agent timeouts, a six-hour batch limit, and no whole-trial retries. The expanded batch retains native timeouts and task resources, with the concurrency and batch limit recorded above. Frozen protocol SHA-256: `33a9e03a0a426b9d1ed8c328f2743ec4efa9b0fdf4425907d4f93dce156aa338`. BixBench-overlap checking is not a prerequisite.

Before SFT, recover available recorded content, validate native-format conversion and loss masks, and count supervised tokens. Keep output limits, repeated tool loops, missing exports, and grader diagnostics as annotations. Pin the selected parent weights and tokenizer, validate the chosen training recipe and long-conversation handling, and freeze the BixBench evaluation protocol. No training or BixBench comparison has run.

## Links

- [Completed Pi collection and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6006473943).
- Logbook: dated updates in this issue; keep this body current as decisions change.
- W&B report: pending the first training run.
- Dataset assessment and known grader issue: [#9630](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9630).
- Biology evaluation protocols and baselines: [#9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258).
- Source project: [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env).

## Decision Log

- 2026-10-05: Start with released Skill2Env biology tasks and complete GLM-only demonstrations. Use native component rewards to select traces and assistant-only SFT. Defer relay methods.
- 2026-10-05: Treat general scientific data analysis as a possible expansion if the validated biology pool is insufficient.
- 2026-10-05: Track this experiment here and link its evaluation results from #9258. Preserve Atlas intake under #9630.
- 2026-10-05: Completed reference/no-op controls on six pinned tasks. Collection: five attempts per task, 30 total. Treat rewards as graded vectors and choose the SFT selection policy after inspecting pilot distributions; this supersedes earlier binary verified-success wording.

- 2026-10-05: Authorized the 30-rollout collection and removed BixBench-overlap checking as a prerequisite. Preserve source provenance and full component rewards.
- 2026-10-05: Superseded Terminus-2 with Pi to match the intended Snowball harness. Selected the paper's 128k context / 32k output teacher budget if supported. Retain the seven prior attempts separately; do not resume their queue.

- 2026-10-06: Completed the 30-attempt Pi batch with 29 native reward vectors and 17 normal trace candidates. Preserve all native scores and raw captures; keep output-limit endings, timeouts, and the ungraded infrastructure failure separate. SFT selection and training remain pending.

- 2026-10-06: Authorized five attempts for every remaining shortlisted biology task (262 tasks; 1,310 new attempts) while unattended. Selected 64 concurrent rollouts after checking bulk inference guidance and sandbox quota. Preserve every native reward vector and verified private artifacts; defer SFT selection and training.

- 2026-10-06: Recovered the first expanded job's 46 fallback attempts without changing native grades. Continue only the 435 unattempted slots; replace the short capture-close window with a bounded 35-minute wait outside the upload lock. Preserve all prior attempts, including incomplete and ungraded outcomes.

- 2026-10-06: Completed all 1,310 expanded slots without duplicates; all evidence is retained and continuation sandbox cleanup is complete. Keep the issue open for the planned SFT and evaluation stages.

- 2026-10-06: Selected an unfiltered first SFT baseline using all available GLM/Pi solver traces, including truncated and interrupted prefixes; supersedes earlier reward and completeness selection proposals. Preserve scores as annotations and avoid artificial termination targets. GitHub and Discord precedents support a bounded continuation but leave parent, mixture, and hyperparameters open.

- 2026-10-06: Selected September 21 Datakit SFT, biology traces only with no replay, one run at peak LR 1e-4, three epochs, 131,072-token training sequences, and effective global batch 16. Save/export and evaluate the final model only; per-epoch checkpointing was dropped because of model-size overhead.

- 2026-10-06: Confirmed full-parameter SFT with fresh AdamH (betas 0.9/0.95, epsilon 1e-8, weight decay 0, clip 1.0), 3% warmup, cosine decay from 1e-4 to 1e-5, and frozen imported router biases. Start evaluation with BixBench alone; decide on other evaluations after its result.

- 2026-10-06: Selected reconstructed conversations and CoreWeave H100 compute (32 GPUs). Finalized 5,120 windows with 73,894,261 supervised tokens per epoch; batch 16 and three epochs give 960 steps. All 58 preparation artifacts passed full SHA-256 readback. Preserve every available solver output, crop only masked context where necessary, and finish trainer validation before launch.

## Conclusion

Collection and the agreed three-epoch, biology-only SFT run are complete. Pi is the primary evaluation harness because it matches teacher collection and intended deployment. The current Pi/BixBench diagnostic does not establish an SFT improvement: thinking-enabled accuracy was parent 1/5 versus SFT 0/5, and thinking-disabled SFT has only two graded attempts out of five. An unexecuted tool call in the final parsed reasoning field was observed in one of five thinking-enabled parent traces and all five SFT traces. It is a pre-existing failure pattern that appeared more frequently after SFT in this sample; it is not unique to the SFT checkpoint. The small sample and incomplete grading limit any broader accuracy claim.

This experiment is finished at the owner's request. The unresolved cause of the Pi formatting behavior and the three missing thinking-disabled SFT grades are accepted limitations of the final result, not outstanding work under this issue. No further runs or debugging are planned here. Any future experiment would have a separate scope and should use Pi as its primary evaluation harness.

Terminus-2 and synthetic tasks remain secondary diagnostics. The [completed prompt ablation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083809697) accepted 36/36 parent versus 0/36 SFT first responses under the Terminus schema. These findings do not establish a remedy for the primary Pi failures. Results and analysis are preserved, and the final diagnostic inference servers have stopped.

topics.title: [grug] Keep AdamH updates finite on zero-norm matrices
topics.body:
scale_by_adamh projects onto the parameter's Frobenius sphere by dividing by
the updated matrix norm. A zero matrix stays zero through a zero learning-rate
or zero-gradient step, so the division is 0/0 and the update is NaN. Floor
that norm at 1e-10, the same floor the direction step already uses.

Fixes #9054
